readings.title: The starting activity that was not an exam
readings.instruction: Read the passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: Adult learners arriving at a numeracy course worried about a short activity on the first evening. Several assumed that a low score would exclude them. The tutor explained that the activity identified familiar topics and areas needing support. Learners could discuss their reasoning afterwards, and the results were not ranked publicly. One participant who answered slowly described a sound method she used at work. This helped the tutor see knowledge that speed alone would have hidden. The activity became a starting point for teaching rather than a judgement of whether learners belonged in the room.
knowledgePoints: 阅读理解：篇章结构与信息判断

readings.title: Feedback that named the next action
readings.instruction: Read the passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: After reading her assignment, a tutor wrote 'develop this idea' beside one paragraph. Farah wanted to improve it but did not know what development meant. At the next meeting, the tutor explained that the paragraph stated a claim without an example. He asked her to add one relevant case and show how it supported the claim. Farah revised the paragraph and then found a similar weakness elsewhere. The useful part of the feedback was not simply that it identified a problem. It made the next action clear enough for her to attempt independently.
knowledgePoints: 阅读理解：篇章结构与信息判断

readings.title: A skill used with unfamiliar numbers
readings.instruction: Read the passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: In a workplace course, learners watched a tutor calculate delivery costs in a spreadsheet. Most could repeat the demonstration using the same figures. When given a different order, however, some copied the old total rather than changing the calculation. The tutor asked them to explain which cells represented distance, quantity and price. Learners then worked on several varied examples. The aim was not to make the exercise harder for its own sake. Changing the surface details revealed whether they understood the underlying relationship and could use it beyond the original demonstration.
knowledgePoints: 阅读理解：篇章结构与信息判断

readings.title: The value of explaining a mistake
readings.instruction: Read the passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A language tutor invited learners to bring one sentence they had corrected during the week. Instead of simply reading the improved sentence, each person explained the choice that had caused difficulty. One learner confused a completed past event with an experience connected to the present. Discussing the difference helped the group understand why either tense might be appropriate in a different context. The tutor avoided treating every error as evidence of carelessness. Many mistakes showed a reasonable rule being applied too widely. Examining the reasoning gave learners a more precise rule to use next time.
knowledgePoints: 阅读理解：篇章结构与信息判断

translation.stem:
Translate the following passage into Chinese:
Useful feedback does more than point out a weakness. It helps a learner see what to try next and why that action may help. When advice is too general, even a motivated learner may struggle to use it. A specific example can connect the advice with the work in front of them. Over time, learners may begin to recognise the same issue and make improvements without waiting for someone else to point it out.
knowledgePoints: 英译汉：语义准确与中文表达
translation.explanation: 注意does more than、even让步强调及without waiting的表达。
translation.referenceAnswer: 有用的反馈不只是指出不足。它帮助学习者看清接下来可以尝试什么，以及这样做为什么可能有帮助。当建议过于笼统时，即使积极的学习者也可能难以运用。一个具体例子可以把建议与他们眼前的任务联系起来。随着时间推移，学习者可能开始自己识别同类问题，并作出改进，而不必等别人来指出。

writing.stem: Write 100–150 words in English about a skill you would like to learn as an adult. Explain why it is useful, describe a realistic practice routine, and explain how you would know you were improving.
knowledgePoints: 写作：任务完成、组织与语言
writing.explanation: 说明技能用途、可持续练习安排及具体进步标准。
writing.sampleAnswer:
I would like to improve my ability to use spreadsheets at work. I can enter information, but I often rely on a colleague when a calculation needs to change. Understanding the process would help me work more independently.
I would practise for twenty minutes three evenings a week. After watching one short demonstration, I would repeat the task with different figures and explain what each part of the calculation means. I would keep a note of questions to discuss with my colleague later.
I would judge progress by whether I could handle a new example without copying an old answer. Completing a task more quickly would be useful, but being able to explain and check the result would matter more. This routine should fit around my existing responsibilities.
